Many believed it was holy water — a miracle.

Crowds gathered, collecting the water and touching the statue in hope.
No one could explain where it was coming from.

Later, a man investigated and discovered the source:
a nearby bathroom pipe had overflowed, moisture collected inside the wall, and water leaked through the statue.

Instead of praise, his findings sparked outrage.
Religious groups accused him of blasphemy, and he was forced to flee the country.

What people believe… and what’s actually true… don’t always align.

Story Title: ZOMBIE OUTBREAK: I Fortified My Restaurant Barge and Stayed Hidden | Creepypasta

A slow-burn survival horror / creepypasta set during a zombie outbreak on a cold, noisy river. When the waterfront collapses, Orson Sedgewick refuses to get trapped on land. He unties his small restaurant barge, slips into an industrial back channel, and turns a floating diner into a hidden safehouse. This realistic, procedural audio story follows the step-by-step choices that keep him alive: plank barricades on the windows, tarps and insulation against wind, a simple solar setup to stretch battery life, strict hygiene using the onboard bathroom, and a hard pivot from freezer meat to fishing and pantry food as power becomes a daily problem. Expect grounded river survival, practical fortification, tight resource management, and a human threat on the water—desperate boat crews who come like pirates, asking first and taking second.
